correctness.rationale: Local Z rotations change an edge phase by the sum of endpoint angles, so gauge classes are the cokernel of the unsigned incidence map. On an odd cycle that map is invertible over the real phase torus; on an even cycle its one-dimensional integer kernel is generated by the alternating sign vector, giving exactly the flux \(\Phi\). In the trace expansion, a phase-carrying monomial has signed edge-use vector in this kernel. A nonzero multiple requires at least one use of every edge, so moments of order below m are phase-free; at order m only the two alternating orientations occur, each with \(m!\) orderings and local trace one, yielding \(2m!s^m\cos\Phi\). Direct matrix reconstruction for \(C_4\), \(s=1/2\), gave fourth moments differing by exactly \(96s^4=6\) between flux 0 and \(\pi\), and the package verifier independently checks the triangle characteristic polynomial and square-cycle moment.

value.rationale: The source itself identifies phase-shifted cycles as a qualitatively different regime. The audited theorem converts that observation into an exact gauge invariant and pinpoints the first spectral statistic that detects it, while the odd-cycle result shows complete cancellation. final_claim: For the phase-shifted EPR-like Hamiltonian on a cycle \(C_m\), all edge phases are removable when \(m\) is odd, whereas when \(m\) is even the only gauge invariant is the alternating flux \(\Phi\); all spectral moments below order \(m\) are flux-independent and \(\operatorname{Tr}((-H)^m)=P_m(s)+2m!s^m\cos\Phi\), so the even-cycle spectrum genuinely depends on flux for \(s>0\). The triangle spectrum is the stated phase-independent eight-point multiset with gap \(2(1-s^2)\).
limitations: The exact first flux-sensitive moment is proved for a single cycle, not general graphs with several independent cycles.
The triangle gap formula is for the Hamiltonian normalization used in the source.
